title: Timed theft layer for mode 1 (derive the trailing/anchored budget from a theft rate plus a chain-relative reaction-delay hypothesis)
goal_statement: Give mode 1 a mirror of KeyStealingScheduleTimed's timed I3 (`horizon_budget_of_timed`): derive the EXACT budget hypothesis the mode-1 client theorems already consume from (a) a rent rate, (b) a per-window recent-theft-producer census, and (c) a new named REACTION hypothesis, rather than assuming the joint budget outright. Time-stamped thefts reuse `stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop` and `stolenOf` from `KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:90` verbatim (`Stolen := stolenOf stolenAt`); no new theft-timing vocabulary is invented. Answers to the item's questions, all confirmed against source: (1) THE EXACT CONSUMED BUDGET SHAPE is not one fixed shape but one theorem (`MoltPetit.Model.budget_of_reaction`) GENERIC in an arbitrary window guard `guard : Nat → Prop`, because every consumer in the codebase (the core anchored theorems and all four Molt client theorems) already carries its OWN guard and the underlying union-bound/exposure-census argument never inspects the guard's shape (`horizon_budget_of_timed`'s proof only ever uses `hu : H ≤ u` opaquely). Instantiated at `guard u := A.slot + 1 ≤ u + n` it is byte-identical to the core anchored form `∀ u, A.slot + 1 ≤ u + n → (badSlotsIn (badKeyrotOn n Δconf rented (stolenOf stolenAt) c₀) u n).card ≤ maxByzantine n` that `honestSlotsUnique_keyrot_anchored` (KeyStealingHorizonCore.lean:258), `keyrot_recent_tip_ancestor_agreement_anchored` (KeyStealingHorizon.lean:134) and `keyrot_recent_tip_ancestor_mem_anchored` (KeyStealingHorizon.lean:222) take as `hBudgetFrom`, with `c₀` the LOWER accepted chain (`stripSigs sc`, always the first chain — the same asymmetric convention `badKeyrotOn` already forces, per `mode1-chain.md`'s gotcha (2)); instantiated at `guard u := now < u + n + H` / `now < u + 5 * n` / `now < u + F + 4 * n` it is byte-identical to the `hBudget` hypothesis of `client_refresh_rule` (Molt/Rotation.lean:267) / `sync_rule`+`sync_rule_mem` (Molt/ClientRule.lean:238,284, at `Δconf := n`) / `max_sync_period` (Molt/MaxSync.lean:176) respectively — so composing needs no restatement of any of the four, only substituting the derived term for their `hBudget` argument. (2) WHAT `theft_is_recent` BECOMES: there is no analogue derived from a structural axiom, because mode 1's floor `inForce` (KeyRotation.lean:72, read off `c₀`'s `confirmedPrefix`) carries no period the way mode 2's flagship schedule `s / R` does — `mode1-chain.md` states outright that 'a theft_is_recent analogue needs a relation between inForce and real time that does not exist yet'. So the healing/backward-locality content that `theft_is_recent` DERIVES for mode 2 is instead ASSUMED for mode 1 as a new named operational hypothesis `Reacts` — playing the role `NoPrematureTheft`/`ErasureTimed` already play (named, not reduced) rather than the role `theft_is_recent` (derived) plays — stating that once a reaction delay `d` has elapsed past a theft's real time `r`, the confirmed floor read off `c₀` has moved strictly past the stolen version: `stolenAt i j r → ∀ s, r + d ≤ s → j < inForce n Δconf c₀ i s`. (3) THE DERIVATION IS PER ACCEPTED CHAIN, confirmed necessary: `badKeyrotOn` is keyed to a fixed witness chain `c₀` (KeyStealing.lean:47), so `Reacts` is likewise parametrized by that same `c₀` (unlike mode 2's `s / R`, which is chain-independent) — composing with a client theorem instantiates `c₀ := stripSigs sc`, the SAME chain the theorem's own `hBudget`/`hBudgetFrom` already reads its census from; there is no chain-independent form. (4) ONE-LINE READING of the derived hypothesis: 'at most `T` producers are, per guarded window, exposed by a theft that has not yet had `d` slots to show up as a floor-raising confirmation on the accepted chain — a reaction-delay-bounded census in place of mode 2's schedule-period-bounded one, still future-inclusive (a theft counted at window `u` stays counted at every later window before `r + d`, never subtracted once healed) but no longer retroactively unbounded provided `Reacts` holds.'

new_defs.name: MoltPetit.Model.Reacts
new_defs.signature:
def Reacts (n Δconf d : Nat) (c₀ : Chain) (stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j r, stolenAt i j r → ∀ s, r + d ≤ s → j < inForce n Δconf c₀ i s
new_defs.meaning: The mode-1 REACTION hypothesis, playing the role NoPrematureTheft/ErasureTimed play in mode 2 (a new named operational assumption, not derived): a reaction delay `d` after a theft of producer `i`'s generation-`j` key at real slot `r`, the floor `c₀` confirms for producer `i` has moved strictly past `j` at every later slot `s ≥ r + d` — i.e. the emergency rotation is confirmed on the witness chain within `d` slots of the theft. Contrapositive form (what the subset lemma below actually uses): if `inForce n Δconf c₀ i s ≤ j` (the theft is STILL live at `s`, i.e. `theftOn` holds there), then `s < r + d` — the theft's real time is within `d` of `s`. `c₀`-parametrized because `inForce` is chain-relative; composed with a client theorem, `c₀ := stripSigs sc`, the same chain `badKeyrotOn`/`hBudgetFrom` already read from. Deliberately NOT reduced to anything about `NoPrematureTheft`-style provisioning periods, because mode 1's `inForce` floor has no period the way mode 2's `s / R` schedule does (`mode1-chain.md`: 'a theft_is_recent analogue needs a relation between inForce and real time that does not exist yet').

new_defs.name: MoltPetit.Model.recentTheftProducersK
new_defs.signature:
noncomputable def recentTheftProducersK (n d : Nat) (stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop) (u : Nat) : Finset Nat :=
  (Finset.range n).filter (fun i => ∃ j r, stolenAt i j r ∧ u < r + d)
new_defs.meaning: The mode-1 mirror of `recentTheftProducers` (KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:149): producers hit by a theft whose real time `r` is within `d` of window `u` (`u < r + d`). Unlike mode 2's census there is NO generation-floor conjunct analogous to `u / R ≤ j` — mode 2's floor conjunct is itself noted as 'redundant under NoPrematureTheft' (ScheduleTimed.lean:137-148), and mode 1 has no period to define an analogous floor from at all, so this census is exactly the reaction-delay-bounded window filter with nothing else attached. Future-inclusive in the same sense as mode 2 (a counted theft at `r` stays counted at every window `u < r + d`, and is never subtracted once the reaction actually fires — `Reacts` only says the corruption HEALS at `s ≥ r + d`, it says nothing that would shrink this census below `r + d`).

new_theorems.name: MoltPetit.Model.exposedProducers_subset_recentTheftK
hypotheses: {n Δconf d : Nat} (hn : 0 < n)
{c₀ : Chain} {stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop}
(hReacts : Reacts n Δconf d c₀ stolenAt)
(u : Nat)
new_theorems.conclusion: exposedProducers n Δconf (stolenOf stolenAt) c₀ u ⊆ recentTheftProducersK n d stolenAt u
new_theorems.proof_sketch: Direct mirror of `exposedSched_subset_recentTheft` (KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:156-172), with the arithmetic-division argument replaced by the `Reacts` contrapositive: `intro i hi; unfold exposedProducers at hi; obtain ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi; rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hs; obtain ⟨hsIco, j, hle, r, hr⟩ := hs -- unpacking theftOn's ∃j, ≤j ∧ Stolen(=stolenOf stolenAt, itself ∃r, stolenAt); rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hsIco; have hslt : s < r + d := by by_contra hcon; push_neg at hcon; have := hReacts _ j r hr s hcon; omega -- `this : j < inForce n Δconf c₀ (producerForSlot n s) s` contradicts `hle : inForce ... ≤ j`; refine Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_range.mpr (by unfold producerForSlot; exact Nat.mod_lt _ hn), j, r, hr, by omega⟩ -- the final `u < r + d` from `hsIco.1 : u ≤ s` and `hslt : s < r + d`.` No division/multiplication reasoning at all (mode 2's `window_producer_inj`-adjacent arithmetic is not needed here — the theft floor is a bare inequality, not a periodic schedule), so the proof is shorter than its mode-2 counterpart.

{guard : Nat → Prop} {Rrent T : Nat}

This item's Honest-scope paragraph documents the same residual W3b is scoped to close: `Reacts` still lets a theft be counted at every window before `r + d` regardless of when any block was actually minted (future-inclusive within the reaction window), because there is still no mint-time EUF-CMA surface. A time-aware signature surface (W3b) would let a future item tighten `Reacts`'s conclusion from 'the floor has moved' to 'no signature under `j` exists after `r + d` was minted', shrinking the census further; W3a does not require W3b and stands alone.

risks.risk: The `guard : Nat → Prop` genericization of `budget_of_reaction` is a design choice beyond the planner's literal working hypothesis (which sketched the derivation at the fixed anchored guard only); if a reviewer wants the item scoped EXACTLY to the anchored form with no generalization, the four Molt `*_timed` wrappers would instead need `anchored_budget_of_reaction` composed through an extra omega-conversion step at each call site (mirroring how `client_refresh_rule` itself converts its own `hBudget` argument today), which is mechanically easy but adds ~4 extra `have`/`omega` lines per wrapper.
risks.mitigation: The generic form is strictly more general (the anchored form is the one-line corollary `anchored_budget_of_reaction`, kept as a named deliverable exactly as asked), so no information or the planner's named shape is lost; implementers preferring the narrower reading can drop the generic `budget_of_reaction` and inline the anchored form four times instead, at the stated proof-line cost.

risks.risk: The exact `#print axioms` output (axiom set and single-line vs 3-line wrap) for the seven new theorems is asserted by analogy with their closest existing siblings, not measured — a real build could reveal an unexpected extra axiom (unlikely, since every ingredient is already guarded at [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], but not certain until built) or a different column-wrap.
risks.mitigation: Both new guard files' outlines explicitly instruct the implementer to probe with a bare `#print axioms` first and copy the emitted message verbatim, per the codebase's own established discovery idiom (results-molt.md).

risks.risk: `Reacts` is a genuinely new named hypothesis with no existing paper term (`docs/rollout/designs-partial/W3a-run2.md` confirms zero grep hits for 'reaction' in paper/molt.tex or the design docs) — a deployment-facing reviewer may object to introducing an unmotivated new primitive assumption rather than reducing it to something already stated.
risks.mitigation: The item's own goal_statement and the module docstring explain why no reduction is possible with the current chain model (inForce has no period, unlike mode 2's s/R); this is recorded as the leading open_questions_for_owner item so naming/motivation can be settled before or alongside implementation, without blocking the Lean content.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Derive a `theft_is_recent`-style backward-locality THEOREM for mode 1 from some periodic provisioning assumption analogous to `NoPrematureTheft`, instead of introducing `Reacts` as a primitive named hypothesis.
alternatives_rejected.why: Mode 1's floor `inForce` (KeyRotation.lean:72) has no period the way mode 2's flagship schedule `s / R` does — there is no 'generation provisioned at `j * R`' structure to hang a derivation on. `mode1-chain.md` states outright that the needed inForce-to-real-time relation 'does not exist yet'; inventing one would require new chain-level machinery well beyond this item's additive scope (an explicit announcement-to-confirmation timing theorem), so `Reacts` is assumed directly, mirroring how `NoPrematureTheft`/`ErasureTimed` are themselves named rather than derived in mode 2.

alternatives_rejected.alt: State the budget derivation at the fixed guard `H ≤ u` (literally mirroring `horizon_budget_of_timed`), requiring each of the four Molt consumers to omega-convert at their own call site.
alternatives_rejected.why: `horizon_budget_of_timed`'s proof never inspects the guard beyond calling `hRent u hu`/`hTheft u hu` opaquely, so genericizing over an arbitrary `guard : Nat → Prop` costs nothing extra in the proof and delivers strictly more: one theorem, `budget_of_reaction`, serves the core anchored form AND all four Molt trailing forms with literally zero restatement, which is a stronger reading of the planner's own 'no restatement' requirement than a fixed-guard version would satisfy.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Attach time-stamped theft to the existing `KeyStealingExecution`/`StolenMint` structure (KeyStealing.lean:101), which already carries a `steal_bad` bridge from minted blocks to bad real slots.
alternatives_rejected.why: That structure is consumed ONLY by `keyStealing_refines_timed` (mode1-chain.md open item (7)), which is not on the path to any client theorem — `client_refresh_rule`/`sync_rule`/`max_sync_period` consume `badKeyrotOn`/`badKeyrot` through a bare `Stolen : Nat → Nat → Prop`, with no reference to `KeyStealingExecution` anywhere. Wiring through it would add an unrelated, unused bridge for no payoff toward the planner's stated deliverable.

open_questions_for_owner: Is `Reacts` the right name/framing, given 'reaction' appears nowhere in the current paper or design docs (confirmed: zero grep hits)? An alternative like `ReactionBound`/`TheftHeals` might read better once this gets a paper section, but the Lean content is independent of the name.

Should a fifth wrapper, `stay_recent_client_safe_timed` (mirroring `Molt.stay_recent_client_safe`, Molt/ClientRule.lean:174, the general-Δconf predecessor `sync_rule_timed` specializes), be added even though the planner's explicit consumer list names only sync_rule/sync_rule_mem/client_refresh_rule/max_sync_period? Does the owner want the generic `guard : Nat → Prop` form of `budget_of_reaction` (this design's choice) or a fixed-guard form closer to the planner's literal working hypothesis (see risks)? Both are fully specified above; the generic form is recommended but is a design decision worth confirming before implementation.
hypothesis_verdict: CONFIRMED, with one simplification found. The planner's working hypothesis is correct on every load-bearing point verified against source: the theft-counts-at-slot-s reading (`inForce n Δconf c0 i s ≤ j`) matches `theftOn` exactly (KeyStealingBudget.lean:42-43); `Reacts` as stated (`stolenAt i j r → r + d ≤ s → j < inForce n Δconf c0 i s`) is exactly what makes the contrapositive argument in `exposedProducers_subset_recentTheftK` go through, mirroring `exposedSched_subset_recentTheft`'s structure step for step; the derivation genuinely must be per accepted chain (`badKeyrotOn` is chain-keyed, `Reacts` inherits the same `c₀`); the anchored/trailing budget derivation from `hRent + hTheft` (guarded identically) `+ hRT` mirrors `horizon_budget_of_timed` step by step with no structural surprises. One simplification versus the planner's sketch: `recentTheftProducersK` needs NO generation-floor conjunct analogous to mode 2's `u / R ≤ j` (which the mode-2 module itself calls 'redundant' under `NoPrematureTheft`) — mode 1 has no period to define such a floor from, and `Reacts`'s conclusion is already fully general in `j`, so the filter is exactly `∃ j r, stolenAt i j r ∧ u < r + d`, simpler than the planner's phrasing might suggest by analogy with mode 2.
recommendation: Build as designed, in the order: MoltPetit/Model/KeyStealingTimed.lean first (self-contained, only needs KeyStealingBudget.lean + KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean, both already landed) and its guard file, confirming axiom sets with a bare #print axioms probe before writing the guard blocks; then Molt/SyncRuleTimed.lean (four thin wrappers, each a single call to an existing Molt theorem with one argument substituted) and its guard file; then the two import-line edits, in that order so `lake build MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingTimed` / `lake build Molt.SyncRuleTimed` can be checked standalone before wiring into the default build. No loop risk: every reused interface (sync_rule, sync_rule_mem, client_refresh_rule, max_sync_period, and the core anchored theorems) is already landed and stable, and this item changes no existing hypothesis anywhere.
